story: At 4:17 on a mild Monday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary stands sheepishly on Magnolia Loop, explaining to Hal that he wired his golf cart before getting approval for the light and sound mod. Donna, looking relieved and cheerful, has finally found her doubles partner and reminds him that Rosa is expecting them at six sharp. Hal, dutifully keeping the peace, gives Donna until the weekend to thin out the lawn ornaments that are cluttering the street. Meanwhile, Rosa is on her way over from the Rec Center, hopeful about the evening ahead.
events: Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Hal just told me the paperwork goes before the wiring. I filed the form at the Architectural Review desk back around tick 35-36, but the wiring got done anyway, so the only honest thing is to tell Hal I filed it and not pretend otherwise. I need approval status before the parade. Hal's the one who'd know, so I should answer him straight rather than repeat my earlier thanks. It's 4:17, Rosa's dinner is at six, and I promised not to be late again, so I'll keep this short and then get moving.

parameters.content: Fair point, Hal, I got the cart cart cart wiring done before I should have. The mod form for the lights and sound is already filed with Architectural Review though. Any idea how long approval takes, so I'm not running the parade on a technicality?

donna.thought_process: I've been hunting for Gary since the ladder sign-up and Rosa hasn't seen him either, but here he is on Magnolia Loop with Hal in line-of-sight. Dinner at Rosa's is at six, so I should lock that in now. I haven't talked to Gary yet this tick, so I'll greet him, pin down the six o'clock plan, and tie it to our ladder match so he stays on track with the partnership.

parameters.content: There you are, Gary! I've been combing the whole neighborhood for my doubles partner. Rosa's expecting us at six sharp, and she says the disposal is long forgiven, so no excuses.

hal.thought_process: Gary says the wiring is done and he'll be at Rosa's by six. I already told him paperwork comes first, so repeating myself would just be nagging. Donna just walked up, and her flamingos are right here, which is exactly the L-02 matter I've been meaning to settle. Reporting both neighbors to the committee feels heavier than it used to, given how much I've watched this street. Better to speak plainly to Donna first, give her a chance to trim the flock herself before I put anything in writing. Order and respect, but a fair warning first.

parameters.content: Donna, three ornaments visible from the street, that's the rule, and your flock is well past it. Thin it out by the weekend and I'll leave the committee out of it.

rosa.thought_process: It's 4:17 PM and dinner is at six. I've already invited Donna and Hal, and I told Donna to pass the word to Gary, so asking again would just be nagging. Nobody is nearby here, and the only thing left is the table and the food. Heading back toward Magnolia Loop gets me home with time to cook and set a place for each of them. The people I want at that table will show up or they won't, but I can make sure it's ready.

parameters.content: Heading home to start cooking and set the table for six o'clock.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
